newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 28.

text.p: Row brews over new fire service chairman: The government is to appoint Roger Estall, a director of international insurance broking firm Marsh McLennan, as chairman of the Fire Service Commission this week despite a row brewing for weeks about the appointment. Page 1.

Super debate not on National's agenda: The divisive superannuation debate would not be on the agenda for the three-day National Party annual conference because the caucus did not have common position on the issue, party president Geoff Thompson said on Sunday. Page 2.

Telecom dismisses cost study findings: Telecom said on Sunday it did not see the relevance in the findings of a study for the Commerce Ministry showing that line leasing costs in New Zealand were higher than in other countries. Page 13.

CHH heading back to court: Forestry giant Carter Holt Harvey is heading back to the High Court in a case that has significant implications for the "amalgamation" provisions of the 1993 Companies Act. Page 14.
Rata's death raises tourist driver issue: Tighter controls on tourist drivers were called for as Maori activist Matiu Rata's body headed for its final resting place today.
Torching signals flaring of gang war: A powderkeg of gang tension enveloping much of the upper North Island is set to blow as Nomad members seek revenge for the slaying of an associate in Auckland.
Scheme no risk to firms' super: Businesses do not see the government's proposed compulsory retirement savings scheme as a replacement for existing company schemes.
Post box key to tax-return ruling: When is a tax return officially returned? When it hits the Inland Revenue Department's post box, according to a ruling by the Taxation Review Authority.
